audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats Subjugate as scarce next to Realm of Death — 'hold Subjugate as a panic button', 'do not initiate with it', 'track its cooldown the way you track his R' — and never gives either number.
audit.why: Realm of Death is 140/120/100. Subjugate is 120/100/80. Trundle's ultimate is back exactly twenty seconds earlier at every rank, so it is the more available of the two, not the scarcer one. The reactive-cast advice is still right for the Realm itself, but the reason changes completely: the player is not rationing a rare cooldown, they are choosing when to spend the one they will have again first. That is the difference between playing scared and playing on a timer.
audit.corrected: Realm of Death 140/120/100 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — yours is back twenty seconds sooner at every rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: Indestructible is described only as a shield that 'absorbs the flat damage of your Chomp' and gives 'sustained healing'. The clause that decides the lane is never stated, and Darkness Rise is absent from both layers entirely.
audit.why: Indestructible 'stores damage he deals AND takes to create a shield. He may consume the shield to heal.' So every Chomp Trundle lands is partly building the shield he then has to chew through, and the shield converts into a heal on command — which makes Grievous Wounds a real purchase, not an afterthought, and the content layer never mentions anti-heal at all. Darkness Rise matters for the same reason: it switches on after three attacks or spells against a champion and gives him a damage aura plus move speed, so the extended trade Frozen Domain is built to force is exactly the trade that turns it on.
audit.corrected: Indestructible stores the damage he deals AND the damage he takes into a shield he can cash as a heal — your chip helps pay for it, so bring Grievous Wounds. Darkness Rise switches on after three hits and adds an aura plus move speed to every long trade.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mordekaiser.json (P Darkness Rise; W Indestructible, cd 12/11/10/9/8, shield + heal)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] says Chomp's 'AD steal and AS debuff reduce his Q slam damage'.
audit.why: There is no attack-speed component anywhere in Trundle's kit except Frozen Domain's buff on himself — Chomp saps Attack Damage and briefly slows movement. Telling the player their bite is cutting his attack speed invites them to trade longer than the Chomp actually justifies, which is the worst possible instinct into a champion whose passive rewards the third hit and whose shield grows on damage taken.
audit.corrected: Chomp is a flat 3.5s attack reset that saps Attack Damage and briefly slows. There is no attack-speed debuff to lean on.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] says 'trade only when his E is down' and early says 'play just outside his E range, bait the cast' — with no cooldown and no range on Death's Grasp, and none on Obliterate either.
audit.why: Death's Grasp is 16/14/12/10/8 at 700 range. Sixteen seconds at rank 1 is one of the longest non-ultimate cooldowns in the lane and genuinely is the window the entry gestures at, but it halves to eight by rank 5 — so 'trade when his E is down' is good advice at level 3 and almost meaningless at level 13. Obliterate runs the other way, 8/7/6/5/4, so his isolated slam gets twice as frequent over the same period. Realm of Death is a 650-range cast, which is the number that defines where the player is allowed to stand at 6.
audit.corrected: Death's Grasp 16s at rank 1 falling to 8s, 700 range. Obliterate 8s falling to 4s. Realm of Death casts from 650.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mordekaiser.json (Q cd 8/7/6/5/4 range 675; E cd 16/14/12/10/8 range 700; R range 650)

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Trundle, Trundle, then Skill for the remaining five stages, and it contradicts the prose at both ends. win[1] reads Trundle while whys[1] underneath says 'he wins the short trade now' and early says 'the lane turns against you at level 2'. win[6] reads Skill while late opens 'Past two items the matchup flips' and whys[6] describes Trundle ending the duel.
audit.why: The packet has 49.01% over 353 games and MC_WR_TABLES reads 45.98, so a chart that never names Mordekaiser at any stage is under-selling him. The entry's own shape is clear and defensible: Level 1 Trundle on the flat 3.5s bite, Levels 2 through first item Mordekaiser as Indestructible and Death's Grasp come online, and two-plus items Trundle once Subjugate has real resistances to take.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Trundle; Levels 2 through first item Mordekaiser; two-plus items Trundle. win[1] should read Mordekaiser and win[6] should read Trundle.

audit.why: The entry's central read on Obliterate holds up and is worth keeping: Riot's text says the damage 'is increased when hitting a single enemy', so the isolated slam is real and Death's Grasp exists to create the isolation. The advice to stand outside the pull rather than to react to it is the right conclusion; I only attached the 700 range and the 16s so the player can act on it.

edits.before: At level 1 Chomp contests his last-hits and the AD steal limits how hard his Q can slam you, making the opening exchange a genuine coin flip — take it if you are already in W range, skip it if you are not. The lane turns against you at level 2 when he has Q plus W: his shield absorbs the flat damage of your Chomp and his Q isolated-bonus kicks in the moment you step close, so short trades start going his way. At level 3 the E pull is the real danger: if he catches you in max-range E the full Q isolated combo comes out before you can Pillar, and his W shield eats your retaliatory Chomp. Play just outside his E range, bait the cast, then step in to Chomp and immediately Pillar behind him to deny his disengage.
edits.after: At level 1 Chomp contests his last-hits on a flat 3.5s, making the opening exchange a genuine coin flip — take it if you are already in W range, skip it if you are not. The lane turns against you at level 2 when he has Q plus W: Indestructible builds its shield out of the damage he deals AND the damage he takes, so your own Chomp helps pay for it, and Obliterate's isolated bonus lands the moment you step close. At level 3 Death's Grasp is the real danger — caught inside its 700 range, the full isolated combo comes out before Pillar resolves. It is 16s at rank 1, so play outside it, bait the cast, then step in to Chomp and Pillar behind him.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are the worst stretch of this matchup. His Q stacks in rank, his W shield scales with AP, and your Frozen Domain healing does not keep pace with the burst he lands on every E-into-Q rotation. At level 6 you cannot confidently all-in him: if you drop Subjugate on him he will immediately pop Realm of Death, bringing you into a 1v1 where he steals your stats back on top of his already-stolen resistances, your W does not follow you into the Realm, and his W shield regen gives him sustained healing you cannot match. The correct play at 6 is to hold Subjugate as a panic button — use it if he pops R on you to immediately drain his stolen resists back and make the Realm fight winnable, but do not initiate with it. Farm safely, match his wave, and let him waste Realm of Death on a non-lethal play before you look for a trade.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are the worst stretch of this matchup. Obliterate ranks from 8s down toward 4s, Indestructible keeps converting the damage you deal into his shield, and Darkness Rise switches on after three hits or spells — a damage aura and move speed layered onto exactly the extended trade Frozen Domain is built to force. At 6 you cannot confidently open: Subjugate him and he answers with Realm of Death, taking a portion of your stats in a 1v1 your W zone stays outside of, then cashing the shield as a heal. Hold Subjugate as the reactive answer — cast it once he pulls you in, to take his resists back and make the Realm winnable. But read the timers: his R is 140/120/100 against your 120/100/80, so yours returns twenty seconds sooner at every rank. Farm, match his wave, and let him spend R on nothing.

edits.before: Past two items the matchup flips. A two-item Mordekaiser has built significant Armor and Magic Resistance and Subjugate now steals a meaningful chunk of both, effectively taking his defensive stats and bolting them onto you mid-fight. Engage outside Realm of Death range with Pillar to cut off his retreat, drop W Frozen Domain to move through him, and open with Subjugate before he can R — the stat swing plus your Iceborn Gauntlet or Trinity Force Chomp damage is enough to burst him without entering the Realm. In teamfights Subjugate onto a stat-stacked Morde makes you effectively unkillable for its duration; peel for your carries and drain him whenever he flanks. He is still dangerous if he lands R on you with Subjugate down, so track its cooldown the way you track his R.
edits.after: Past two items the matchup flips. A two-item Mordekaiser has real Armor and Magic Resistance, and Subjugate takes a percentage of Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft across four seconds — his defence bolted onto you mid-fight. Engage from outside Realm of Death's 650 range, Pillar to cut his retreat, drop Frozen Domain, and open with Subjugate before he can R. Your ultimate is 120/100/80 against his 140/120/100, so it returns twenty seconds sooner at every rank — the window is far more often yours than the panic-button framing suggests. Keep Grievous Wounds on him, because Indestructible spends its stored shield as a heal. In teamfights drain him whenever he flanks and peel for your carries.

notes: BIGGEST ADD: Indestructible 'stores damage he deals AND takes to create a shield' and can be consumed to heal. Both layers described it only as a shield that absorbs Chomp, which hides the actual instruction — the player's own chip is building the shield, and it converts to a heal on command. That makes Grievous Wounds a core purchase, and the content layer never mentioned anti-heal once. SECOND ADD: Darkness Rise is absent from both layers. It turns on after three attacks or spells on a champion and gives him a damage aura plus move speed, which means the extended Frozen Domain trade Trundle is told to force is the exact trade that switches it on. COOLDOWN FIX: the entry treats Subjugate as the scarce resource — 'hold it as a panic button', 'track its cooldown the way you track his R'. Realm of Death is 140/120/100 against Subjugate's 120/100/80, so Trundle's ultimate is back twenty seconds sooner at every single rank. The reactive cast is still correct, but for the opposite reason to the one implied. ADDED NUMBERS: Death's Grasp 16s at rank 1 falling to 8s at 700 range (the window whys[3] gestures at, and it halves as the game goes), Obliterate 8s falling to 4s, Realm of Death casting from 650. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: (1) the entry says Chomp's AD steal 'limits how hard his Q can slam you' — the kit file gives no scaling ratios, so I removed the AD-steal justification from wants.you[0] where it was paired with a non-existent attack-speed debuff, but did not assert the opposite anywhere. Whether Obliterate scales with attack damage at all is not answerable from the kit files. (2) 'your W does not follow you into the Realm' — plausible and widely believed, but Riot's text for Realm of Death says only that he drags the victim to another dimension, so I kept the entry's existing phrasing rather than strengthening it. (3) breakdown.cooldowns claimed Death's Grasp carries 'passive magic pen'; Riot's description says only that it pulls, so I did not restate the claim in the rewrite. NOT EDITED (enum): win[1] reads Trundle directly above a whys[1] saying 'he wins the short trade now', and win[6] reads Skill above a late paragraph opening 'Past two items the matchup flips' — win[1] should be Mordekaiser and win[6] Trundle.
